facts.title: Marathi Language Heritage
facts.english: Marathi is one of the oldest regional languages in India with literary heritage dating back to around 1000 CE.
facts.description: The Marathi language has a rich literary tradition including works by saints like Dnyaneshwar and Tukaram, and modern writers like Pu La Deshpande and Vijay Tendulkar.

facts.title: Ganesh Chaturthi Festival
facts.english: Ganesh Chaturthi is a 10-day Hindu festival celebrating the birth of Lord Ganesha, widely celebrated with special fervor in Maharashtra.
facts.description: During this festival, homes and public spaces install clay idols of Ganesha, offer daily prayers, and on the final day immerse the idols in water bodies with grand processions.

facts.title: Warli Painting Art
facts.english: Warli painting is a tribal art form originating from the North Sahyadri Range in Maharashtra, known for its simple geometric shapes depicting daily life.
facts.description: This ancient art form uses basic shapes like circles, triangles, and squares to represent humans, animals, trees, and houses, creating beautiful narrative scenes.

facts.title: Lavani Dance Form
facts.english: Lavani is a traditional Maharashtrian dance form known for its powerful rhythm and energetic movements, traditionally performed to the beats of Dholki drum.
facts.description: Originally performed by women to entertain soldiers, Lavani combines song and dance, often presenting social themes with wit and humor.

facts.title: Maharashtrian Thali Meal
facts.english: A traditional Maharashtrian thali (platter) typically includes bhakri (millet bread), varan (lentil stew), amti (spicy lentil), rice, pickle, papad, and sweet.
facts.description: The thali represents a balanced meal with carbohydrates, proteins, vegetables, and sweet - reflecting the agricultural diversity of Maharashtra's regions.

festivals.name: Ganesh Chaturthi
festivals.description: 10-day festival celebrating Lord Ganesha's birth, featuring idol installation, daily puja, and visarjan (immersion) processions.

festivals.name: Diwali
festivals.description: Festival of lights celebrating the victory of good over evil, involving lamp lighting, fireworks, sweets exchange, and Lakshmi puja.

festivals.name: Gudi Padwa
festivals.description: Marathi New Year festival marking the beginning of the Chaitra month, celebrated by hoisting Gudi (flag) outside homes.

food_items.name: Puran Poli
food_items.description: Sweet flatbread stuffed with jaggery and chana dal (split chickpeas) paste, often eaten during festivals and special occasions.

food_items.name: Vada Pav
food_items.description: Iconic Mumbai street food consisting of a deep-fried potato dumpling (vada) placed inside a bread bun (pav) with chutneys.
food_items.serving_style: Served hot with fried green chilies

food_items.name: Misal Pav
food_items.description: Spicy curry made from sprouted moth beans (matki) topped with farsan (sev, onions, coriander) and served with pav (bread).
food_items.serving_style: Always served with lemon wedge and extra sev on top

landmarks.name: Shaniwar Wada
landmarks.description: 18th-century fortification in Pune that served as the seat of the Peshwa rulers of the Maratha Empire until 1818.
landmarks.significance: Political center of Maratha Empire, witnessed important historical events including the assassination of Peshwa Narayanrao.

landmarks.name: Gateway of India
landmarks.description: Iconic monument built during the British Raj in Mumbai, overlooking the Arabian Sea, built to commemorate the landing of King George V and Queen Mary.
landmarks.significance: Symbol of colonial power, later became symbolic of Indian independence as last British troops departed from here in 1948.

landmarks.name: Ajanta Caves
landmarks.description: UNESCO World Heritage site featuring 30 rock-cut Buddhist cave monuments dating from 2nd century BCE to about 480 CE.
landmarks.significance: Masterpieces of Buddhist religious art, featuring paintings and sculptures depicting Jataka tales and Buddha's life.

etiquette_tips.title: Greeting Elders
etiquette_tips.description: When greeting elders in Marathi culture, it's respectful to slightly bow your head or do a namaste gesture with hands together.
etiquette_tips.context: Meeting grandparents, teachers, or anyone significantly older
dont: Call by first name without permission

etiquette_tips.title: Footwear Removal
etiquette_tips.description: It's customary to remove footwear before entering someone's home, temples, and many traditional establishments as a sign of respect and cleanliness.
etiquette_tips.context: Homes, temples, some restaurants, traditional shops

etiquette_tips.title: Dining Etiquette
etiquette_tips.description: When dining with Maharashtrian families, wait for the eldest to start eating, use your right hand for eating, and compliment the food.
